lessons.title: Temporary Routes and Building Access
lessons.objective: Learners will understand and correctly use remain in effect and step-free access in workplace notices.

reading.text: The city transport team will close Market Street to buses from 8 p.m. Friday while crews repair a damaged drainage cover. Route 6 will use Oak Avenue in both directions; the diversion will remain in effect until inspectors confirm the road is safe. Digital signs at three stops will show the temporary route, and drivers will announce the change before leaving the central station. The team will review passenger reports on Monday and adjust the notice if any stop information is unclear. Passengers who need step-free access should check the updated stop map, because two temporary stops have no raised platform.

sentences.text: The city transport team will close Market Street to buses from 8 p.m.
Friday while crews repair a damaged drainage cover.
Route 6 will use Oak Avenue in both directions; the diversion will remain in effect until inspectors confirm the road is safe.
Digital signs at three stops will show the temporary route, and drivers will announce the change before leaving the central station.
The team will review passenger reports on Monday and adjust the notice if any stop information is unclear.
Passengers who need step-free access should check the updated stop map, because two temporary stops have no raised platform.

targets.meaningEn: to continue to be valid or active until changed or cancelled
the ability to enter or move through a place without using steps or stairs
targets.meaningVi: lối đi không có bậc thang

exercises.prompt: In sentence s3, what does remain in effect mean when the diversion will remain in effect until inspectors confirm the road is safe?

options.text: The diversion will continue to be active until inspectors change it.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches continuing to be valid until changed.

options.text: The diversion will stop immediately and will not wait for inspectors.
options.explanation: Wrong because it describes immediate cancellation instead of continuation.

options.text: The diversion will stay listed on a notice even after buses stop following it.
options.explanation: Wrong because remaining listed is different from remaining active for buses.

exercises.explanation: The diversion stays active until inspectors confirm safety.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence using remain in effect.

options.text: The temporary safety rules will remain in effect until the manager updates them.
options.explanation: Correct because the verb form and time clause are natural.

options.text: The temporary safety rules will remains in effect until the manager updates them.
options.explanation: Wrong because remains should be remain after will.

options.text: The temporary safety rules will remain in effect to the manager updates them.
options.explanation: Wrong because to should be until before a clause.

exercises.explanation: Only the correct sentence uses the phrase with natural grammar.

exercises.prompt: In sentence s6, what does step-free access mean when passengers who need step-free access should check the updated stop map?

options.text: It means passengers can use a route without paying a fare, even if it has stairs.
options.explanation: Wrong because free in this phrase does not mean that a journey costs no money.

options.text: It means passengers can enter and move through the stops without using steps.
options.explanation: Correct because it matches moving without steps or stairs.

options.text: It means passengers can reach the platform only by using a ramp, not a level path or lift.
options.explanation: Wrong because step-free access does not require one specific route such as a ramp; it means there are no steps or stairs.

exercises.explanation: The phrase refers to moving without steps or stairs.

exercises.prompt: Choose the correct sentence using step-free access.

options.text: The new entrance provides step-free access for visitors who use wheelchairs.
options.explanation: Correct because provides agrees with the singular subject, and the phrase is used naturally.

options.text: The new entrance provide step-free access for visitors who use wheelchairs.
options.explanation: Wrong because the singular subject requires provides, not provide.

options.text: The new entrance provides step-free access at visitors who use wheelchairs.
options.explanation: Wrong because at should be to or for before the people who receive access.

exercises.explanation: Only option a has correct subject-verb agreement and a natural construction.

exercises.prompt: You are an office assistant welcoming a job candidate for an interview. Write 2-3 sentences to tell the candidate how to enter the building comfortably. Use the phrase step-free access.
exercises.sampleAnswer: We look forward to meeting you tomorrow. Our main entrance offers step-free access, so you can reach reception without using stairs. Please let us know if you need any extra help.
selfCheck: I used the phrase step-free access correctly.
I describe entering without steps and offer help.
